source_text: So, what I was thinking in connection with the co-op question is really what the customer benefits are.  Like, if I set out to maintain a free/open clone of whatever is coming out of SF these days, that *could* be useful for people IF they could run it on their hardware, i.e., I don't think many people can run a free/open frontier model, but it's worth being careful about this; firstly, some of the items I found, like Mastra, are already open source, and also, I'm not actually *that* keen on creating open source material that I don't personally find useful.  So, maybe rather than trying to discover the problems that Oakland residents might be trying to solve, I can leave that to my friend, and think about the problems that I personally am trying to solve, many of which are written down in capability stars, and see whether any of the technology I learned about could help me with any of those problems.  It may also be a good time to do some introspection and think about whether I have a full list of problems-to-solve and capabilities-to-gain for myself or if my list is somewhat prejudiced.

reply_text:
㊥ (gist) Turning the survey on your own problems gives a clear answer: the technology helps most with **`wm-overnight-unsupervised`**, and the best of it is open. The introspection also suggests the list is somewhat prejudiced, for a structural reason I can point to. Both are in the mission as §4 (`dc69bef`).

㊢ ("whether any of the technology I learned about could help me") I matched the 13 held stars and 1 active star in the star map against the survey. The useful matches:
- **`wm-overnight-unsupervised`**: four things you could take directly, all open.
  - Reticle's verdict spec: yes / no / unknown / no-fault, and it refuses any action that wasn't declared in advance.
  - Zeroshot's separate review-and-repair loop.
  - Smithers' durable runs with rewind.
  - Cotal's leases with fencing tokens.
- **`efe-trustworthy-over-starmap`**: calibrated typed decisions, through the open SGLang + Clef route (needs a GPU).
- **`full-arxiv-mining`** and **`ai-passes-prelims`**:
  - Crawlee for harvesting
  - SGLang for serving open models locally
  - Paritok for using fewer tokens
  - JevOps's pattern of letting Lean decide what gets admitted
- **`hypergraph-operator`**: Cognisee and Scribe Optimize, as things to learn from.
- **`symbol-grounding`**: nothing in the survey.

㊟ (the t2 chain) The revenue chain is stuck at its first link: `cold-eoi-sent` is at n=0, which the star map itself calls "the crux". No tool from SF would send that first email. By the test we used earlier, that's probably not a tooling gap. It's either a missing intent or something blocking it, and only you know which.

🈖 ("somewhat prejudiced") Missions *mint* capabilities. So only something that already has a mission can become a star. That's the same selection effect that tripped up the July probe: the map draws your goals from the apparatus that already exists. All 36 stars fall into five regions: the War Machine, mathematics, the hypergraph, revenue, and the pudding-prover kit. Things you've put real effort into recently that have no star:
- **you learning mathematics faster or better.** The map has "AI passes prelims" but nothing about Joe learning.
- the phone/Kinesis/DeX/voxterm workstation
- infrastructure that survives a drive failure
- money: taxes, filings, the Ltd question, and the decision you face at the end of the year
- teaching, workshops and Peeragogy
- writing and publishing: futon7a, the MMCA paper
- fun: ChipWits
- friends' projects, like the Oakland co-op

🈸 (one decision) Which of these are real goals, and which are maintenance or pastimes that don't need a star? I'd only mint the ones you confirm. The rest stay in the mission as a record that the question was asked.
